resources.string: After the restart, Android keeps the camera, microphone and location off for Pocket Guard until you open it. Tap to open it once: intruder photos, SOS video and location come back.
Tap the round button before you get into a crowd
Put your phone in your pocket or bag
Take it out and unlock to use it normally
Unlock now or the siren starts
Unlock the phone to stop the siren
Time to unlock before the siren: %1$d s
Quiet siren, for trying it at home. Turns itself off after 1 hour.
Warns if it\'s unplugged while locked, e.g. charging at a café
Warns if your earbuds or watch lose the phone while it\'s out of your pocket and locked
Offer to arm when earbuds connect
Earbuds in usually means you\'re on the move. A notification asks; one tap arms.
Offer to arm on bus or train
Uses Google activity detection (cars too). A notification asks; one tap arms.
None ticked means any earbuds, headphones or watch
No paired earbuds or watch found
Earbud triggers need the Nearby devices permission.
Auto-arm needs the Physical activity permission.
Takes 2 silent front-camera photos when the siren starts. Saved only on this phone, for when you get it back.
Alarm can show on lock screen
What the guard saw and decided, newest first. After a test, tap Copy and send it to the developer.
Nothing yet. Arm the guard, lock the phone and test.
Cover the top of the screen with your hand to test.
Turn on Test mode. Tap the round button on Home, lock the phone.
Put it in your pocket. A short buzz means it\'s protected (half a second after locking).
Take it out without unlocking: after 2 s it beeps (in your earbuds if connected).
Wait: the quiet siren starts, the torch flashes, photos are taken.
Unlock with your fingerprint or PIN: everything stops and it re-arms.
Volume buttons during the siren shouldn\'t silence it.
Charging: arm, lock, unplug. Beeps, then the siren.
Armed and locked: turn on airplane mode from the lock screen. The siren starts. Then check History for the photos.
Pocket Guard screams the moment your phone leaves your pocket without your fingerprint, while the thief is still next to you.
Tap the round button on Home or the Quick Settings tile, then pocket your locked phone. A short buzz means it\'s protected. Take it out and unlock within 2 s: no sound.
Beeps in your earbuds, then a siren the thief can\'t silence, a flashing torch and photos of whoever is holding it. Restarting the phone doesn\'t stop it.
Set it up, then test it
Next, allow what the alarm needs: each one is a single tap. Then turn on Test mode in Settings to try it with a quiet siren.
Pocket Guard turned itself off after 4 hours armed automatically.
Pocket Guard needs a screen lock (PIN, pattern or password) to tell you from a thief.
On a bus, train or in a car? Tap to arm Pocket Guard.
Earbuds connected. Tap to arm Pocket Guard.
Android stopped Pocket Guard. Tap to arm it again, and allow it in battery settings.
Set a screen lock (PIN, pattern or password) first
The phone wasn\'t locked when this started, so unlocking won\'t stop it. Open Pocket Guard, tap the round button on Home and confirm it\'s you.
Siren can override Do Not Disturb
Turn off Smart Lock / Extend Unlock: while it keeps the phone unlocked, unlocking can\'t prove it\'s you.
Time to unlock before the siren: none, siren at once
With no delay, your own pull-out also sets off the siren unless the phone is already unlocked.
Siren if someone turns on airplane mode while it\'s locked, to cut it off the network
Intruder photos need the Camera permission.
Locks immediately when the screen turns off
Settings → Lock screen / Security: \"Lock after screen timeout\" = Immediately, and \"Power button instantly locks\" on. Tested every time the screen turns off while armed.
Not tested yet: arm the guard and let the screen turn off by itself once. Set \"Lock after screen timeout\" to Immediately and turn on \"Power button instantly locks\".
Password needed to power off (if your phone has it)
Your phone didn\'t lock when the screen turned off, so a thief could get it unlocked. Tap to set \"Lock after screen timeout\" to Immediately.
Something in the alert changed since you approved it. Tap to review and approve it again.
Confirm it\'s you to stop the alarm
What sets off the alarm while armed
Arms by itself at the times you set and turns off at the end, like a Focus schedule.
Turned off inside a scheduled time, it pauses for 15 min and then arms again. Skip today keeps it off until that time ends.
Arms within a few minutes of the set time. Allow \"Alarms & reminders\" for the exact minute.
Pocket Guard is paused. It arms again at %1$s.
Your scheduled time ended, so Pocket Guard turned off.
Your schedule couldn\'t arm Pocket Guard by itself. Tap to arm it.
Taken out of pocket or bag
Proximity, light and motion sensors decide. Always on while armed.
Delete all alarms with their intruder photos and SOS recordings? This can\'t be undone.
Android blocks these by default. Without the required ones the alarm may never sound. Each takes one tap; come back here after each screen.
A PIN, pattern or password, so the app can tell you from a thief.
Set \"Lock after screen timeout\" to Immediately and turn on \"Power button instantly locks\".
Shows that the guard is on and lets the alarm reach the lock screen.
Stops battery saving from switching the guard off in your pocket.
Shows \"THIS PHONE IS STOLEN\" to whoever holds it.
Your phone brand stops apps restarting. Turn Autostart on for Pocket Guard.
Takes intruder photos when the siren starts.
Lets the siren sound even in total silence mode.
Call for help without opening the app: tap volume up 4 times quickly.
Records video with sound while SOS runs.
The people who get your location by SMS (and email) when you start SOS.
Lifting, tilting or pushing it off warns. Unlock when you pick it up.
This person called for help. Please stay with them, or call the local emergency number.
SOS: tap volume up 4 times quickly

While armed, with the screen on (locked or unlocked, so waking it with your fingerprint is fine): tap volume up 4 times within 2 s. Not while music, a video or a call is playing. A loud whistle and a spoken call for help, and it records video with sound until you unlock.

SOS: while armed, wake the screen (a fingerprint unlock is fine) and tap volume up 4 times quickly: a buzz, a whistle and a spoken call for help, and recording starts. Unlock to stop; the video is in History.
Slide, lift or tilt it and it warns, silently for the first 1.5 s so you can unlock. Two short buzzes mean it is guarding the table.

On a table: lock it and lay it down (face-up or face-down). Two short buzzes: guarded (face-up about 1 s, face-down about 4 s). Slide, lift or tilt it: beeps after 1.5 s. Lift it and put it back down still: they stop.
Lets Pocket Guard see volume up tapped 4 times quickly, to sound the SOS alarm. It only watches the volume buttons: it reads nothing on screen and every button works as usual.
To use the SOS buttons, turn on \"Pocket Guard SOS buttons\" in Accessibility.
Android protects this setting for apps installed outside the Play Store, so it takes three steps. Each button takes you to the right screen; come back here after each.
Tap the switch for Pocket Guard SOS buttons. Android says it is restricted: tap Close.
In App info, tap ⋮ (top right), then Allow restricted settings, and confirm.
Turn on Pocket Guard SOS buttons.
Recording needs the Camera and Microphone permissions.
Recording people without their consent is against the law in some places.
Saved %1$d to your gallery (Pocket Guard album).
Couldn\'t save to the phone. Check the free space and try again.

Pocket Guard uses the Accessibility service to detect volume up tapped 4 times quickly, to start the SOS alarm and recording, even on the lock screen and when the app is closed. It only watches the volume buttons: it does not read your screen, collect what you type, or change any settings, and the buttons keep working as usual. Nothing it sees leaves your phone. You can turn it off any time in Accessibility settings.

Pocket Guard uses the camera to take photos of whoever is holding your phone when the theft siren starts, even when the app is closed or the phone is locked. The photos stay on your phone, in History, where you can delete them.

Pocket Guard uses the camera and microphone to record video with sound when you start SOS, until you unlock, even when the phone is locked. The recordings are saved on your phone, in History. When your SOS alert with the live location link is on, the video is also uploaded so the people you approved can watch it from that link; otherwise you choose if and with whom to share it.

Pocket Guard uses the names of your paired Bluetooth devices so you can pick which earbuds or watch count, to warn you when they lose the phone and to offer arming when they connect. This stays on your phone.
Pocket Guard uses physical activity (being on a bus or train) to remind you to arm the guard, even when the app is closed. Nothing is stored or shared.
Also from the lock screen: the SOS button on the Pocket Guard notification, or the SOS tile in Quick Settings.
When you start SOS, these people get your location by SMS (and by email, if you add an address), 5 s later unless you cancel, then updates if you move.

When you start SOS, an SMS with your location is ready for these people 5 s later (unless you cancel): tap Send SMS and send it from your messages app. People with an email address get it by email by themselves.
Approved: %1$d people get this when you start SOS.
Alerts are off until you approve the message and the people. Tap to review.
Nobody here can get an alert yet: add a phone number (or an email address with online features on).
Enter your name for the alert first.
In English letters: Bangla letters make every SMS part hold less than half as much, so each alert would cost twice the SMS.
When you start SOS, Pocket Guard will send this SMS to %1$s, %3$d seconds later unless you cancel, and an update if you move:\n\n%2$s

When you start SOS, Pocket Guard will prepare this SMS to %1$s, %3$d seconds later unless you cancel. Tap Send SMS to open your messages app with it filled in, then send it; tap again later for the newest location:\n\n%2$s

If you move, updates read: %1$s
If you stop SOS right after it goes: %2$s

Pocket Guard uses your location only while SOS is running, to put it in the alerts to your emergency contacts (and on the private live map their link opens, when that is on), even when the phone is locked. It is not used at any other time.

Pocket Guard uses your location only while SOS is running, and sends it by SMS from your phone to the emergency contacts you approved (and to the private live map their link opens, when that is on), even when the phone is locked. It is not used at any other time.
%1$s needs help! SOS from Pocket Guard at %2$s. Location: %3$s (within %4$d m)
%1$s needs help! SOS from Pocket Guard at %2$s. Location not available yet, an update follows.
Test from Pocket Guard, nothing is wrong. An SOS alert would read:
%1$s er shahajjo dorkar! Pocket Guard theke SOS, %2$s. Location: %3$s (%4$d m er moddhe)
%1$s er shahajjo dorkar! Pocket Guard theke SOS, %2$s. Location ekhono pawa jayni, update ashche.
Pocket Guard theke test, kichu hoyni. Ashol SOS alert emon hobe:

While SOS runs, your location and the video it records are also shared through Pocket Guard\'s server: the message carries a private link to a live map with the recordings, which works until a day after SOS ends. People with an email address get the alert by email too. Shared locations and videos are deleted after 90 days.
During SOS, share your location and the video it records through Pocket Guard\'s server, with a link your contacts can follow, and email the contacts who have an address. Off: SMS only.
Deletes this phone\'s anonymous account and every location and video it shared.
Delete everything Pocket Guard stored online for this phone? Live links you already sent stop working.
Deleted. Nothing from this phone is stored online.
Couldn\'t reach the server. Try again when you\'re online.
